items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: When I spoke of hearing Charlie Johnson's orchestra for the first time, I forgot to mention that Jimmy Harrison, the great trombonist, was in the band. But the night I heard it, I don't remember him having any solos.

ctx.x: Sidney told me that he was surprised to see me playing trumpet and with the Scott brothers whom he had known when they had been in New York before. He also told me that here had been changes in the musicians that had been with Charlie Johnson. Jabbo Smith had left. He and Leonard Davis had been hired and Edgar Sampson had taken Benny Carter's place.

When I spoke of hearing Charlie Johnson's orchestra for the first time, I forgot to mention that Jimmy Harrison, the great trombonist, was in the band. But the night I heard it, I don't remember him having any solos. Jimmie was

not in good health and the one thing I noticed was that he held a hand on his stomach when he was not playing. Jimmy was replaced by George Washington which made 3 musicians of the Arthur Gibbs orchestra that joined Charlie Johnson after the Scott band went into the Savoy, Jimmy Harrison died in July, 1931.
